chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Norman Granz and Jazz at the Philharmonic
summary: Brown praises Granz for paying hundreds more than others, though he is unsure where Castle Rock was recorded.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Did a lot of recording and played a lot of different places. Went to Europe. Played a tour with our great, great friend, Norman Granz.
And Norman really liked the band. And he did everything he could to help us.
Well, at that time, Norman still had a great deal of influence -- didn't he?
In which -- what do you mean?
Oh sure, he still has. Yes --
After awhile he pulled out of it and when he was in Europe he --
Well he kind of retired. Yeah. But

Oh yes, Norman is -- I'll always give Norman all the credit I think I can because to me he's one of the greatest men to ever be an agent. When nobody else was paying them anything, he was paying them hundreds more than anybody would pay them.
I think you mentioned some of these earliest presentations here in Los Angeles -- what were the [big -- you went to (inaudible)].

Well, at that time -- the first time I ever heard of Norman a fellow -- $200.00 working in the band would be tops. And here come Norman Granz with his Jazz at the Philharmonic and those kind of places -- he was paying six and $700, which was unheard of.
Of course that drew every decent musician in the country trying to get with Norm Granz. But he -- he's worth it. He really treats them royally if he likes you.
Yeah, Duke used to -- when they were getting along --
And he recorded a great many people and he put together combinations --
-- of musicians that hadn't been heard anywhere else.
